How good are the 603 selected OLI endmembers?

19 October 2026 · Internal fixed-library diagnostic; not independent validation

Assessment

Useful category signal, but not an abundance-validated endmember library. The selected pixels improve nearest-reference category agreement compared with random pixels from the same polygon footprints. However, they cover within-category variation less closely, many selected spectra admit other-category reconstructions, and the screened synthetic unmixing experiment beats a three-category prior but does not beat a dense five-category prior. This does not establish that an exhaustive MESMA search or every possible use of the library would fail. It does identify substantial concerns before abundance use.

What was supplied and verified

The array has 85,706 observations × seven undarkened OLI channels. All values are finite, none are negative and all five recorded categories are represented. The CSV contains 603 unique zero-based column indices, confirmed by the user. Those references come from 367 polygon identities; one polygon contributes as many as 19 selected pixels. No selected spectra are exactly duplicated.

The label file stores category names. The user's numeric mapping is preserved as the separate class_code field, never confused with array indexing:

Code Recorded category Selected spectra Selected polygon IDs Nearest-reference recall Cross-category hull matches
1 Deciduous 115 55 46.6% 42/115
2 Evergreen 166 116 87.3% 80/166
3 Herbaceous 90 62 45.3% 54/90
4 Non-vegetated & dead 141 79 77.3% 11/141
5 Woody shrub 91 55 40.3% 36/91

The supplied spectra align, in original row order, with the repository polygon Parquet's undarkened OLI columns divided by 10,000 (maximum absolute difference 7.46e-8, compatible with numerical precision). Every category label matches. This establishes usable numerical lineage; it does not independently validate physical units, pure materials or native Landsat observations.

The imagery_year field differs from source acquisition dates on 18,399 rows. This report derives acquisition years from flight_id; it does not rewrite the original field or assume that the field necessarily means acquisition year.

What you see: every selected trace, grouped by recorded category, with a dark median. What to notice: there is considerable within-category variation and unequal category/parent coverage. Segments connect discrete bands. What it means: selecting 603 rows is not equivalent to sampling 603 independent plants. What it does not mean: labelled polygons are verified pure materials or these seven-band synthetic representations are independent Landsat measurements.

1. Coverage and category discrimination show a trade-off

For each polygon/site/acquisition-year, take within-flight medians, then the median of those flight summaries. Exclude every one of the 367 candidate polygon IDs globally. This leaves 3,272 polygon IDs / 4,261 summary curves. Repeated identity histories share total weight one in aggregate results. These targets are disjoint from the chosen references, but selection already examined the entire library, so they are not selection-blind holdouts.

The control draws 30 alternative libraries. Each preserves exactly the selected pixel count from each same polygon ID. Category counts, parent identities and per-parent capacity are therefore matched; only the chosen pixels change. Controls may by chance include supplied selected pixels. This comparison isolates pixel selection within these polygon footprints, not selection of different polygon footprints.

  • Mean nearest same-category spectral RMSE: selected 0.01507; matched random mean 0.01159. Selected distances are 30.0% larger (worse coverage by this metric).
  • Nearest single-reference category agreement, balanced across categories: selected 59.4% versus random mean 55.6%. Random-draw central 95% spread is 53.2–57.3%.
  • Evergreen recall is 87.3%, whereas Woody shrub is 40.3% and Herbaceous 45.3% under this particular raw-band nearest-reference rule.

A stricter follow-up also preserves the selected pixel count from each same polygon and flightline, preventing changes in acquisition composition. Its 30 random controls average 0.01256 for same-category RMSE and 54.8% for nearest-reference balanced agreement. The broad coverage/discrimination trade-off remains; both sets of controls are saved. This does not make either comparison selection-blind.

Spectral RMSE is in supplied-array units. This is a descriptive proximity rule, not the earlier nested classifier, not MESMA abundance and not deployment accuracy. The result is compatible with selecting more discriminating references at the cost of representing typical within-category variation. The selector's exact objective/script was not supplied, so its intended optimization cannot be judged.

What you see: selected pixels versus 30 matched random libraries, by category. What to notice: selection improves some category recalls while coverage worsens. What it means: quality depends on whether the goal is discrimination or reconstruction. What it does not mean: the random-draw ranges are population confidence intervals or this internal comparison is independent confirmation.

What you see: confusion between recorded labels and performance by acquisition domain. What to notice: category difficulties differ; the overall average hides failures. What it means: all categories and domains should remain visible during evaluation. What it does not mean: these are held-site models: the original selection saw all sites.

2. The selected library contains concrete category ambiguity

For each selected spectrum, exclude every reference with its own category. Solve a full-library linear feasibility problem: can a nonnegative, sum-one combination of the other categories reconstruct the same seven-band vector? Numerical certificates are accepted only after separately checking spectral RMSE ≤1e-8, nonnegativity and sum-one constraints.

223 of 603 (37.0%) have verified alternatives. Herbaceous has 54/90 (60.0%), Evergreen 80/166 (48.2%), and background/dead 11/141 (7.8%). Thus even a perfect reconstruction can disagree with the recorded one-hot category interpretation of a reference.

This feasibility diagnostic permits multiple references per category and as many as eight active references in seven-dimensional affine space. It is broader than three-component, one-reference-per-category MESMA. Failure to find such a certificate does not prove uniqueness, especially for mixed targets or noisy data. All 223 certificates and their actual reference indices/weights are saved.

What you see: certificate counts and one concrete target/alternative reconstruction. What to notice: the spectra overlap, while the category weight vectors differ. What it means: this dictionary does not guarantee unique category composition. What it does not mean: the LP alternative is known biological truth or is admitted by the more restrictive screened MESMA experiment.

The selected library's affine spectral rank is seven. With 603 references, unique individual-reference fractions cannot generally be recovered from seven bands and one sum constraint. That dimension argument alone does not prove category ambiguity; the explicit certificates supply the category-level evidence here.

3. Synthetic recovery improves on a matched sparse prior

Use eight disjoint parent bundles, two in each observed site/acquisition-year cell, with one distinct parent per category. No generating parent occurs in the selected library or another bundle. Generate 45 mixtures per bundle: ten category pairs at fractions 0.1/0.5/0.9, ten equal-third triples, and five pure-parent targets. This gives 360 known algebraic mixtures, not 360 independent plants or field plots.

For each target, screen the three closest references per category from all 603 selected spectra using spectral RMSE only, never the known fractions. The existing numerical solver then searches 375 admitted models, at most three categories, with nonnegative sum-one fractions. A full unfiltered search would have 16,918,447 such candidate models per target and was not run. Consequently this tests a screened inference configuration, not exhaustive full-library MESMA. Solver rank/interior/update tolerances remain those of the existing spectralbridge.mixtures.fit_models implementation.

Model / control Fraction RMSE
Selected screened MESMA 0.322
Matched random screened MESMA 0.313
Uniform design prior 0.304
Sparse design prior 0.345
Known-parent FCLS oracle 0.000

The oracle is approximately 3.6e-14: correct generating parents recover the synthetic truth. The selected configuration's 0.322 does not beat the uniform 0.304 prior. The prior is fixed at 0.2 per class from the symmetric design, not fitted using test fractions. One matched random library gives 0.313; that is one draw, not a population-level claim about random selection superiority.

RMSE above is sqrt(mean squared error over targets and categories). For clarity, mean per-target RMSE gives selected 0.293, random 0.283, prior 0.292: aggregation matters, but it does not reveal a selected-library advantage over the dense prior in this experiment. These values are not directly interchangeable with previous mean-fold synthetic-study headline RMSEs.

Whole-bundle bootstrap intervals are conditional on eight sampled bundles and this synthetic recipe. Resampling uses the observed domain mixture and does not model spatial correlation between nearby polygons. Treat these intervals as internal sensitivity summaries, not independently validated population coverage. The selected-minus-prior RMSE difference is 0.018, with conditional 95% percentile interval 0.004 to 0.034. The selected-minus-one-random-draw difference is 0.009, interval -0.007 to 0.025. These are internal sensitivity summaries, not geographic/field validation.

What you see: selected and control errors plus calibration by true fraction. What to notice: the oracle succeeds, whereas the selected configuration does outperforms the sparse prior but not the dense prior; absent classes receive positive predictions. What it means: accurate spectral reconstruction is insufficient for fraction recovery. What it does not mean: every MESMA configuration must fail or any result validates field cover.

A constraint-matched prior changes what we can conclude

MESMA outputs at most three nonzero category fractions. The dense prior uses all five. A follow-up fairness control therefore assigns 1/3 each to the first three predefined categories and zero to the others, without inspecting any target spectrum or selecting categories from outcomes. Under this balanced synthetic recipe any fixed triple has the same aggregate error. Its fraction RMSE is 0.345. MESMA's 0.322 improves on that sparse baseline, so the spectra add some quantification information under the same sparsity limit.

The stronger dense prior predicts the design expectation, while MESMA searches for a spectrally fitting sparse composition. These are different objectives and output constraints. Failing to beat the dense prior alone is not evidence of a broken solver or proof that the selected library contains no useful information. Neither comparison establishes accurate, unique biological abundance. The sparse control was added after reviewing this potential confound, not presented as a preregistered experiment.

Detection and quantification are different failures

At the explicit comparison threshold predicted fraction ≥0.10, absent-class false detections are common. A low positive fraction is defined as 0 < truth ≤0.20. Thresholds are comparison rules, not independently measured physical detection limits.

Category Fraction RMSE False positive when truly absent Miss at low positive fraction
Deciduous 0.337 53.8% 62.5%
Evergreen 0.303 63.0% 46.9%
Herbaceous 0.362 46.2% 62.5%
Non-vegetated & dead 0.247 30.8% 62.5%
Woody shrub 0.345 45.2% 50.0%

Screening and near-fit sensitivity

After the primary run, repeat with 1, 2 and 5 screened candidates per class. Fraction RMSE is 0.336 / 0.328 / 0.316, respectively, versus the primary three-candidate 0.322. More candidates improve fit and some fraction error, but none beats the dense design prior here; all improve on the sparse prior. These exploratory checks do not establish what the full 16.9-million-model search would do.

At additive near-fit tolerance 0.01 array RMSE, the primary search has mean 17.8 near-fitting category sets (out of 25), with median maximum category fraction range 1.0. Reducing tolerance to 0.001 gives mean 4.5 near sets. These tolerances are illustrative, not calibrated sensor noise. The existing solver saves one best solution per category set: ranges are restricted candidate ambiguity, not exhaustive feasible or biological uncertainty.

What you see: fraction error as screening expands, and near-set count as tolerance expands. What to notice: conclusions depend on the evaluated search and tolerance. What it means: both inference design and library ambiguity must be reported. What it does not mean: a selected operating point is universally optimal or near-set ranges are confidence intervals.

Recommended next step

Keep this as a candidate reference dictionary, but do not describe it as validated for category abundance. Obtain the selector script/objective and repeat selection inside training-only polygon/site folds. Evaluate unmixing on parent-disjoint target curves, compare matched parent/library capacities, and retain failed controls. For the frozen whole-library selection, independent new observations are needed for selection-blind performance. Field abundance additionally requires independent, contemporaneous fractions at matched spatial support and verified reference meaning.

Reproducibility and limits

preflight.py records the initial ambiguity before the user clarified indexing; summary.json is the current confirmed analysis. run_analysis.py reads the three original files and the existing Parquet in place. No source file is changed or copied. selected_members.csv and target_coverage.csv preserve reference/target IDs. Figures are regenerated from compact results by build_report.py. Input/code hashes, the 30 controls, every LP certificate, synthetic parent memberships, predictions, per-class errors and bootstrap summaries are retained in this packet. No earlier scientific outputs, production algorithms or coefficients were changed.
